content: The image shows a close-up of corn kernels with white/cottony mold growing between them. Kernels appear tan to pinkish-salmon colored with fluffy white mycelium. This points to an ear rot disease. Key candidates: Fusarium (white-pink cottony mold scattered on kernels) vs Ear_rots_Diplodia (white mold from base).

The test image shows pale cream/salmon-colored kernels with white fluffy cottony mycelium filling the spaces between kernels — consistent with Fusarium ear rot description: "white to pink or salmon-colored cottony mold on single or multiple kernels...on the ear." The kernel color (pinkish-salmon, not yellow) and scattered cottony white mold match Fusarium well. The reference image confirms scattered white mold patches on kernels.
